title: Quick Start: Marvelous Designer Ui (1)
description:
Welcome to the new Quick Start tutorial series.  Are you ready to elevate your sewing game and unlock endless possibilities in fashion design? Then hit the play button, and let's get started!

By the end of this tutorial, you'll be well-equipped with the knowledge to navigate around the User Interface of Marvelous Designer.

summary: ```markdown # Quick Start: Marvelous Designer UI Welcome to the quick start tutorial on the UI of Marvelous Designer. In this tutorial, we will explore various features and functionalities available in the software. ## Mouse Settings Let's start by checking our mouse settings. Select **Preference**, then **View Controls**. You have the option of changing to different presets. Find the one that fits you best, or create a custom one. In the Preference menu, you can also find the configuration of other aspects that involve the function of the software. ## Interface Overview On the left side of our screen, we have two different tabs: **General** and **Connect Store**. ### General - The **General** tab contains the main distribution of the software. ### Connect Store - If you click on **Connect Store**, you will access it directly from the software. You will need to log in with your unified account. - Here, you will find useful content distributed in four categories. The content can be from other users, and the Connect team will provide many free items. This can help beginners access quality patterns, poses, trims, and fabrics without leaving Marvelous Designer. ## Window Layout The default distribution of Marvelous Designer is as follows: - On the left side is the **3D Window**. - On the right side is the **2D Window**. - On top of the 3D window are the **3D Tools**. - On top of the 2D window are the **2D Tools**. The **Library** is located on the left side of the 3D window, where you can access files from the different default folders. Under the library, you can display the files within the selected folders. ### Folder Management You have the option of resetting folders, adding folders, or downloading files from them using the icons on the top right of the library. ## Object Browser On the right side of the 2D window, we have the **Object Browser**. This tab provides different options, with **Selected Fabric** being the default. This can be changed at any moment. - If you click on the **Created Fabric**, it will display the **Properties Menu**, where you can find many parameters to work with and achieve the right effect for your garments. ### Hiding Windows If you are not going to use the Object Browser or the library, you can hide them to leave more space for the 3D and 2D windows. You can bring them back whenever needed, or you can add them to the library. ## Workspace Distribution On the lower right side of the screen, you will find four different icons that will change the distribution of the workspace. This allows you to add or remove windows. Each window can be swapped for any other functionality available. To change a window, go to the window you want to change. At the top of it, you will see the specification of which one is active, indicated by an arrow pointing down. You can toggle the window within the main workspace to locate it where it is best for you. To activate this functionality, just click on the top right icon of the desired window. To turn it off, click on the X icon. ## Trim Menus and Properties Now let's access some trim menus and properties. For this, simply select one of the options available. In this case, I will select the **Button Menu**. If you select the active trim, you will access their properties menu, displayed under the trim menu. ## Adding Avatars Let's introduce an avatar into the scene. To do this, click on the **Avatar Icon**. You will need to access your default avatars through the avatar folder in your library. For instance, I open the file of **Hannah**. You can choose from a variety of default avatars, covering male and female options, stylized avatars, and age variations. Each will include motion, pose, and shoe options. Remember that if you need more options, you might find what you need at the **Connect Store**. ### Importing Avatars and Garments You can import either custom avatars or garments into the scene. Go to **File**, then **Import**, and choose the most suitable option from the different formats. If you just want to add to the current scene, you can use the option **Import > Add**. If you have your garment already saved in one of your folders, you can simply drag it into the scene. You can add as many garments or avatars into the scene as you need using the **Import > Add** option. ## Exporting Options If you need to export, you will find a list of different formats to choose from. Each format allows you to set specific properties. ### FBX and OBJ Properties Let's see what **FBX** and **OBJ** properties look like. Both formats have options to set the type of mesh, the behavior between patterns, maps, and UVs that are the same, but they have unique specifications for each format. - **OBJ** allows the user to specify which items are included in the export. - **FBX**, for example, allows us to exclude the rig or keep the animation cache. FBX also allows us to save textures. ## Saving Options When using the save format from Marvelous Designer, you will have to choose between saving as a garment or a project. - **Saving as Project** will keep the garment and the avatar within the file. - **Saving as Garment** will keep only the garment and exclude the avatar from being saved. ## Animation Tools At the bottom of the workspace, you can locate the **Animation Tools**. To open the animation tab, click on the arrow pointing up on the bottom-mid. ## Omniverse Connector The **Omniverse Connector**, one of the bridges of Marvelous Designer, is located in the Object Browser and can be added to the server or join a session from there. Thank you for watching! ```
